title: Hōryū-ji Buddhist monuments
summary: Hōryū-ji, near Nara, is a Buddhist temple founded in 607 by Prince Shotoku. A fire destroyed the original buildings in 670, and rebuilding began almost at once and ran into the early 8th century. Eleven surviving structures date from the late 7th or 8th century, among the oldest wooden buildings in the world. UNESCO inscribed the 48-structure property in 1993.

uncertainty.note: Start is the founding date given by World History Encyclopedia; UNESCO says the original buildings burned in 670 and rebuilding ran into the early 8th century, so the standing buildings are later than the start. End is the present.

reviewer_note: No model: the five-storey pagoda's height (about 32 m in search snippets) was not stated with a plan dimension on any page I could open (the World History Encyclopedia gives only the central column, over 35 m). UNESCO's XML lists two points (Horyu-ji and Hokki-ji, about 1.8 km apart); I used the one that agrees with the OSM Horyu-ji way (about 0.2 km away). The 607 founding date is from World History Encyclopedia only; UNESCO gives no founding year.
